ui/webview stable

An HTML and CSS engine that paints pages into a pixel buffer, takes the window's events, and tells the host what the user did.


The engine draws images through ui/image, which decodes what the platform decodes.

The view is a guest in a window: the host owns the event loop and the surface, the view owns a rectangle of it. Everything in this page is drawn by the engine itself, from the top bar to this sentence, with no JavaScript involved — the DOM is edited from Vertex instead.

The engine is pure Vertex above the platform's fonts and images. A page that renders here renders the same on any display scale.

Embedding

Create a view, give it bounds, load a page, and forward events. Press Tab to move between fields and ⌘C to copy a selection.

let view = webview.WebView()
view.SetBounds(origin: window.Point(0, 52), size: window.Size(w, h - 52))
try view.LoadFile("docs/index.html")
view.OnNavigate { url in try? view.LoadFile(url) }

API

MethodWhat it does
LoadHTML(_:baseURL:)Shows a page from a string; relative references resolve against the base.
Handle(_:)Takes a window event and answers whether it was for the page.
Draw(into:canvasSize:scale:)Paints the view into the window's pixels at the device scale, rounded corners, glyphs and all.
SelectedText()The text the user selected, with a line break where it spans lines.
Resizing the window relays out; it does not restyle unless the page uses media queries or viewport units.

What you get

CascadeSpecificity, inheritance, media queries, pseudo-classes and pseudo-elements.
LayoutBlocks, lines, floats, flex, tables, positioning.
PaintGradients, shadows, images, rounded corners, text decorations.
InputLinks, forms, focus, selection, the clipboard.

Getting a page up

  1. Parse the markup with text/html; the tree is the DOM.
  2. Resolve styles, build boxes, lay them out at the view's width.
  3. Build a display list and rasterize it at the display's scale.
